blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The concept of Biodiversity Hotspots was introduced by Norman Myers in 1988.
A region must contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics to be designated as a hotspot.
A hotspot must have lost at least 70% of its primary native vegetation due to human impact.
India encompasses four major biodiversity hotspots: The Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland.

blocks.content: A biodiversity hotspot must contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics and have lost at least 70 percent of its primary native vegetation.

rows: Greater than 70% primary native vegetation lost
Varies; can be pristine or minimally disturbed

items: Nicobar Islands belong to the Sundaland hotspot, whereas the Andaman Islands fall under the Indo-Burma hotspot.
Western Ghats and Sri Lanka are treated as a unified biodiversity hotspot region.
Norman Myers is frequently asked in competitive exams as the originator of the biodiversity hotspot concept in 1988.
